results.bound: $O(m)$ preprocessing time and $O(\log e(G))$ sorting time and comparisons
results.previous_best: $O(m)$ preprocessing and $O(\log e(G)+m)$ sorting time (Haeupler et al. [14, SODA'25] and van der Hoog et al. [30, SOSA'25]); $O(n^\omega)$ preprocessing and $O(\log e(G))$ sorting time (van der Hoog and Rutschmann [19, FOCS'24])
results.quote: We can preprocess a DAG G on X in O(m) time, so that, given an unknown linear order L on X and the guarantee that all edges in G go from smaller items to larger items with respect to L, we can sort X in O(log e(G)) time and comparisons.
